title: Continuous integration
request: Extend the GitHub workflows: on every push run the full check and the end-to-end flows against a PostgreSQL service container, and build the image on main. No job may use a model key. Cache dependencies. A failing check should block the merge.
spec: On every push: make rd-check and make product-e2e against a PostgreSQL service container; on main, build the image. No model key in any job; dependencies cached; a failing check blocks the merge.
plan: Check whether CI passed on GitHub before the change: it had failed at its Python setup step on every push (it looked for a requirements file that does not exist), so it had never run a test.

Write .github/workflows/ci.yml to replace the old workflow: rd-check, the suite on a PostgreSQL service container (test-pg), product-e2e and the secrets scan on every push, pull request and nightly; on main, a containers job (12.1).
Set an empty OPENAI_API_KEY and DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS=1 for the whole workflow; cache pip by requirements/base.txt and install CPU-only PyTorch.
Push, read each failing run's logs, fix the causes one by one, and mark the package done only when a run passed both jobs.
Leave branch protection to the owner: it is a repository setting.

decisions.decision: Pin mcp below 2 rather than rewrite the MCP server for the new major version.
decisions.why: The code is written and tested against the 1.x decorator API; a new major version installed fresh on CI is an unplanned migration, not a CI fix.

decisions.decision: The development script's database test names CI's scratch database as remote on purpose, instead of loosening the 'this machine only' guard.
decisions.why: CI's PostgreSQL is a service container answering from its own address; the guard refusing it is correct behaviour.

decisions.decision: Do not turn on branch protection from the session.
decisions.why: Making checks required on main is the owner's repository setting; the package records it as open.

change: New .github/workflows/ci.yml replacing rd-knowledge.yml: a check job (rd-check, test-pg on a PostgreSQL 16 service, product-e2e, scan-secrets) on push, pull request and nightly; a containers job on main (compose up --build --wait, the flows against the container, an image secrets scan); no model key; pip cache; CPU-only PyTorch.

findings.defect: On CI nearly every test that builds the app failed, while all passed locally.
findings.scenario: The fresh install resolved mcp>=1.20 to 2.3.0, a new major version that removed Server.list_tools, which the MCP server uses; locally 1.27 was installed.
findings.cause: An unbounded dependency range met a new major release.
findings.test: The second CI run passed the app-building tests.

findings.defect: The development script's database test was refused on CI.
findings.scenario: CI's PostgreSQL service answers from the container's own address, which the 12.0 'this machine only' check rightly refuses.
findings.cause: The test assumed a database on the same machine.
findings.fix: The test names the scratch database as remote on purpose.

findings.defect: The secrets scan failed on CI on values the local scan had not seen.
findings.scenario: tests/test_config.py holds a made-up key and a made-up database password; the local scan reads tracked files only, and the file was not yet committed, so only CI found them.
findings.cause: The scan covers what is tracked; a new test file was untracked locally.
findings.fix: Allow-list the two made-up values by the hash of their value; the scan reports zero findings in the files and the history.

findings.defect: A test waiting for the Home agent's first message in a second workspace failed on CI and never on a laptop.
findings.scenario: On GitHub's runner the draft never got the agent's first message within 30 seconds, and later not within 120. Locally the same test takes about a second.
findings.cause: Not slowness: the signed-in test clients were never entered, so each request ran on an event loop that closes with the response; the Home agent starts as a task on that loop, and on a busy runner the task was cancelled before it began. Under uvicorn the loop outlives the request, so the product was fine.
findings.fix: First the wait was raised to 120 seconds with the draft's state printed on failure (which did not fix it); then the draft is created through the client entered in setUpClass, with the second owner's session.
findings.test: The second-workspace test in tests/test_accounts.py; CI went green after the fix.

measurements.name: CI on GitHub
measurements.gate: A run on main passes both jobs: the check job (rd-check, test-pg, product-e2e, scan-secrets) and the containers job.
measurements.result: Run 37547513100 passed both jobs after two failing runs (first mcp 2.x, the remote-database test and the scan; then the second-workspace wait). The same wait failed again on later pushes until its real cause was fixed.
measurements.next: The owner turns on branch protection for main with the two checks required; a lock file would make CI repeatable.

outcome: Done (482b67b, 24f1dfb, 905e8d0, f7b9b7b; the flaky test's real cause fixed in 532c51f): CI runs the whole check, the PostgreSQL suite, the end-to-end flows and the secrets scan on every push with no model key, and the containers on main. Open: blocking the merge needs main protected by the owner; the dependencies are not locked.
lessons: Check whether the existing CI has ever run a test before extending it; this one had failed at setup on every push.
A fresh install on CI finds what a long-lived local environment hides: unpinned major versions and untracked files.
Raising a timeout is not a diagnosis; a test that takes one second locally and never finishes on CI is usually a lifecycle problem, here an event loop that closed with the request.
